newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late Brent trading yields weaker prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late Brent trading yields weaker prices.

text.p: Late Brent trade Wednesday in the U.S. aftermarket window saw prices retreat on an outright basis, but hold steady for inter-month spreads.
Foreign crude traders said April Brent was sold for a full cargo at $19.56, six cents under the IPE April settlement at $19.62 a barrel.
Other deals saw May Brent switch hands at $19.33, five cents below the IPE settle.
The April/May Brent spread moved at 19 cents, in-line with talk in London that valued the spread at 15-20 cents.
May/June Brent was also traded at 5 cents, again steady from earlier in the session.
